quarterly_data.quarter: Keysight Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Neil Dougherty sized the supply shortfall: with a six-month order acceptance policy, the ~$2B Q2 orders would normally ship by Q4, against a Q4 revenue guide of $1.94 billion, so 'maybe there is $100 million in there that is pushing out beyond our normal shipment window' (probably less, because of deferred software revenue and longer-dated programs). He called it delayed revenue recognition, not lost business. The shortfall is concentrated in '20, 30 SKUs focused on this data center ecosystem', and for some of them 'there isn’t really another equivalent alternative in the marketplace' to double-book. The constrained parts are 'not high-dollar components', so he does not expect gross-margin impact and thinks Keysight could pass on any cost increases. CEO Satish Dhanasekaran said Keysight is now considering acquiring some of its smaller suppliers ('maybe that capability belongs in Keysight') and expects to 'get through it' in a couple of quarters.

quarterly_data.quarter: Keysight Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Interconnect test (optical and electrical) is 'a little over one-fourth of the total business' from an interconnect point of view. 'Right now, copper is the predominant contributor to the business', and management said there is 'more scale to build for the optical side of things' as customers work on complex physics problems.
quarterly_data.figure: a little over one-fourth of the total business

quarterly_data.quarter: Keysight Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The moderator asked whether revenue reaches $2 billion a quarter at some point next year. The CFO said 'certainly that’s the trajectory we’re on', but because of supply constraints the timing of crossing the '$2 billion revenue per quarter threshold is a little uncertain'. The CEO said AI-driven (wireline) demand was strong in the first half and 'the second half could be stronger than the first half, from everything I see today', with both R&D and manufacturing demand rising for the AI data center.
